Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both wake visual views—before touching the policy. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf now, as required for this architecture pass, and record any actual transfer in the candidate notes.

The contract confirms this is a single-candidate edit: policy, provenance notes, and one durable guidance lesson are all mandatory; CFD is explicitly out of scope. I’m now applying the two relevant workspace skills: the visual-first skill determines which views and metrics must be inspected, while the bookshelf skill constrains any mechanism transfer to normalized body-frame feedback.
`rg` isn’t installed in this workspace, so I’m using a read-only file inventory to locate the parent notes, diagnostics, policies, and image sheets. No candidate changes have been made yet.

All four sampled runs satisfy the direct-uniform still-water contract. The strongest finite trajectory is the crossflow-plus-centerline-course policy (`9.880L`, `11.59T`); the prefilled gated anterior redirect is an informative regression (`11.081L` minimum, then receding to `11.155L`). I’m comparing their visual sheets first, then the other two failures to separate shared route topology from mechanism-specific effects.

The inherited notes and the new rollout close two branches cleanly: transient anterior redirect regressed and allowed distance to rebound, while centerline-gated course braking materially improved closest approach (`10.513 → 9.880L`) without changing the upper-exit class. I’m consulting the shelf now for a genuinely different feedback mechanism that preserves the full traveling wave; scalar gain tuning would not meet the transfer protocol or the evidence.

The visual and trace evidence points to a saturation-architecture problem, not missing route magnitude: in the best run, bearing remains negative while yaw flips from `-2.15` at `8T` to `+2.40 rad/T` at `9T`, yet the combined route-plus-yaw command stays near the same `-12°` posterior limit. I’ll preserve the successful crossflow/course route channel and test one new mechanism from the shelf: separately bounded fast yaw-recoil feedback, so observed corrective yaw can actually release the slow route curvature within a beat. I’m recording that hypothesis and its falsification boundary before editing the policy, as the visual-first skill requires.

The candidate will therefore restore the best sampled carrier and change only one feedback mechanism: route curvature and yaw-recoil curvature receive separate smooth bounds before their bounded sum is added to the full posterior wave. This keeps all observations normalized/body-frame, preserves reflection symmetry, and gives the fast response real release authority without changing morphology or episode code.

Both required provenance files are now updated, and the policy contains exactly one candidate. The durable lesson records the parent’s course-brake improvement and the gated-redirect regression without claiming this unevaluated candidate as evidence. I’m checking the final diff and then invoking the mandated workspace check runner; I’ll repair and rerun anything it flags.

The configured check-runner agent could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this Codex account. I’m continuing with the exact three non-CFD commands embedded in that runner configuration, run separately, so the required guidance, policy-contract, and boundary validations still receive their intended coverage.

The first check exposed a workspace metadata defect before reaching my guidance change: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the validator sees two “copied to guidance” markers. I’m removing only that duplicate parent line, then rerunning the exact check; no scientific evidence or policy setting is changing.

The guidance check now passes. The Julia contract command is blocked by the environment rather than the policy (`julia: command not found`); I’m checking the non-login PATH and common installation locations before treating that validation as unavailable. The remaining boundary check is independent and will still run.

No Julia executable exists in the non-login PATH or common installation roots, so the runtime contract check cannot execute here. The boundary check passes. I’m replacing only the unavailable portion with deterministic static guards for parameter-schema completeness and forbidden state/routes, plus a final manual syntax/diff inspection; CFD remains untouched.
A broader read-only search found the workspace’s Julia runtime outside PATH. I’m rerunning the exact configured contract command with that executable, which removes the only remaining validation gap.

All configured non-CFD checks now pass: material guidance/notes, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. An extra lightweight Julia check also confirms reflection equivariance and soft acceleration bounds. I’m doing the final file inventory and line-number pass now; no further mechanism changes are planned.

Produced exactly one policy candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1). It separates slow route curvature from fast yaw-recoil feedback while preserving the full traveling wave.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1), including the required bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:91) with evidence-backed course-brake and anterior-redirect lessons.
- Removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:123) that initially broke validation.

Validation passed: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract, parameter-schema guard, boundary check, reflection equivariance, and acceleration bounds. No CFD was run.
